title: Master Use License (Sound Recording)
summary: License a specific sound recording (master) for use in film, TV, ads, games or online video.
useWhen: A production wants to use the original recording of a song. A sync license for the composition is also needed.
watchOuts: Every recorded song has two separate copyrights: the composition (music and lyrics), usually owned by songwriters and their publishers, and the sound recording or master, usually owned by whoever paid for or made the recording (the artist or label). Licenses and splits for one do not cover the other. A master use license covers only the recording. The composition needs a sync license from the publishers.
Recordings made under union agreements (SAG-AFTRA, AFM) may require new-use fees to performers when used in film, TV or ads. The licensee usually pays these.
If the recording contains samples or featured artists, confirm the master owner has the right to license them for sync.
Check whether the master owner controls the recording in all territories. Distribution and label deals sometimes split rights by territory.

variables.label: Licensor (master owner)
variables.help: Who controls the rights being licensed.

variables.label: Writers or artist
variables.help: Songwriters (for the composition) or recording artist (for the master).

variables.label: Licensor's controlled share
variables.help: Percent of the rights the licensor controls. Other co-owners must license their shares separately.

variables.label: Production title
variables.help: Film, episode, ad, game or video.

variables.label: Type of use
variables.help: How the music is used on screen.

variables.label: Media
variables.default: all media now known or later devised
options: all media now known or later devised
variables.help: Where the production may be shown.

variables.label: Most-favored-nations?
variables.help: Fee increases to match the other side of the song if they get more.

variables.label: Credit
variables.help: On-screen or end-credit wording, if any.

variables.label: Governing law (state)
variables.help: Two-letter code of the state whose law governs this agreement. Usually where the parties or the work are located.

sections.title: 3. License
sections.body: On payment of {{fee}}, Licensor grants Licensee a non-exclusive license to synchronize the Master with the Production, and to reproduce and distribute the Production with the Master. Use: {{use_type}}, up to {{duration}} seconds in total, {{uses}} use(s), in the production "{{production}}" (the "Production"), in {{media}}, throughout {{territory}}, {{term}}. Licensor's controlled share: {{controlled_share}}%.

sections.title: 4. Not included
sections.body: Not included: the underlying musical composition, which needs a separate sync license; soundtrack album use; remixing, re-editing beyond fitting the timing, or altering the Master without written approval; and use outside the Production.

sections.title: 5. Union fees
sections.body: Union recording: {{union}}. If any union or guild requires new-use or reuse payments to performers because of this use, Licensee will pay them, unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.

sections.title: 7. Most-favored-nations
sections.body: If Licensee pays any owner of the composition a higher fee or better terms for the same use, Licensor's fee and terms will be increased to match.

sections.title: 8. Licensor's promises
sections.body: Licensor owns or controls {{controlled_share}}% of the Master in the territory, including any featured performances and samples it contains, and has the right to grant this license. Licensor will indemnify Licensee against claims that the Master infringes another's rights, up to the fee paid.

sections.title: 9. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Massless open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Music rights are split between the composition (song) and the sound recording (master); royalties also depend on PRO, publisher, distributor and label agreements that this template does not change. An entertainment attorney should review deals involving advances, ownership transfers or long terms.
